hero.title: Epigenetic and genetic analyses from one drop

principle.caption: The principle
principle.title: The layer a rapid test does not cover
principle.lead: The six analyses complement point-of-care testing on the Igloo reader with what it does not show: individual predisposition and regulatory processes that change over time.

cards.title: Two layers: genetics and epigenetics
cards.text: Genetic variants describe lifelong, unchangeable predisposition. Epigenetic markers — microRNA patterns and DNA methylation — describe the current regulatory state and respond to nutrition, exercise, sleep and strain. That is precisely why they can be measured over time.

cards.title: Sample material: dried blood card
cards.text: A few drops of capillary blood from the fingertip are applied to a dried blood card. No venipuncture, no centrifuge, no cold chain — sampling is possible in the practice or at home.

cards.title: Laboratory and reference data
cards.text: Analysis is carried out by our cooperation partner, a specialised European laboratory with more than 15 years of research in this field. Results are placed against more than 60,000 validated reference values. Quality management to ISO 9001:2015.

analyses.caption: Portfolio
analyses.title: The six analyses
analyses.lead: Every analysis runs through the same sampling route. What differs is scope, method and the question it answers.

items.name: Metabolic Health
items.subtitle: Which diet suits which person — genetically predisposed, epigenetically verifiable.
items.what: The analysis evaluates which distribution of macronutrients suits the individual predisposition, supported by specific portion and recipe suggestions. Because genetic variants do not explain weight behaviour on their own, epigenetic markers of DNA stability and inflammation are assessed in addition: only those respond to lifestyle and work as a measure of success.
who: Nutritional counselling that needs to go beyond standard plans
Prevention practices running structured weight programmes
Clients for whom previous dietary changes have not worked

items.name: Healthy Aging
items.subtitle: Biological age across four molecular layers — with a traffic-light rating rather than a single number.
items.what: Telomere length, epigenetic ageing markers, inflammation and DNA stability are placed against age- and sex-related reference values and each rated green, amber or red. This shows which layer is driving the result — and where an intervention should start. Lifestyle data is recorded alongside and contrasted with the molecular findings.
who: Longevity centres and prevention practices running structured programmes
Nutritional counselling and doctors working in preventive medicine
People aged roughly 40 and over who want to track their ageing process

items.name: Biological age clock
items.subtitle: An exploratory lifestyle signal from three microRNAs — explicitly not an age determination.
items.what: Three microRNAs are determined by quantitative PCR, normalised against miR-93 and combined into a single value: the percentage deviation of biological from chronological age. The underlying model is published but declared a pilot study — the output is an exploratory signal, not a robust biological age.
who: Longevity and functional medicine practices, as an entry and monitoring parameter
Health centres, coaching and workplace health programmes
As a compact single value where a full ageing panel would be too extensive

items.name: Telomere Analysis
items.subtitle: The protective caps of the chromosomes as a baseline — measured in kilobase pairs.
items.what: Telomeres shorten with each cell division and are regarded as a marker of cellular ageing. Measurement is performed from dried capillary blood, reported in kilobase pairs and placed against an age- and sex-matched reference population. qPCR values vary considerably between runs and laboratories — the trend carries the message, not the single value.
who: Longevity programmes and preventive medicine, as a baseline and monitoring measurement
Nutritional counselling that wants to document an objective starting value
Workplace health programmes with a longevity focus

items.name: Stress Monitor
items.subtitle: Measured strain alongside perceived strain — six microRNAs across four areas.
items.what: Physiological strain, cell protection, serotonin regulation and immune signals are each reported as a traffic light and contrasted with the subjective stress experience recorded in a questionnaire. The discrepancy is what makes the conversation useful: people with high tolerance for strain frequently underestimate their own load.
who: Workplace health management and resilience programmes
Practices and advisory services focused on stress prevention
People under sustained professional or personal strain

items.name: Healthy Sport
items.subtitle: Eight epigenetic areas on the current state — extended in the Plus variant by four genetic variants.
items.what: Nutrient and hydration status, load level, recovery, injury risk, cardiovascular fitness, inflammation and muscle status form the variable monitoring part. The Plus variant adds four unchangeable genetic variants on sport type, training motivation, muscle damage risk and weight regulation — recorded once.
who: Sports medicine practices and performance diagnostics
Sports science, coaches and performance coaching

workflow.title: How it works in your practice

Sampling: prick the fingertip, apply blood to the card, let it dry.

evidence.caption: Evidence base
evidence.title: What is established — and what is not
evidence.lead: This field is heavily over-promised. Anyone presenting these analyses should know the limits — otherwise they collapse at the first critical question. With professionals, candour is an advantage, not a risk.

established.title: Lifestyle changes epigenetic markers
established.text: Randomised pilot trial over 8 weeks: epigenetic age on average 3.2 years lower than in the control group (Fitzgerald et al., Aging 2021). This measured DNA methylation, not microRNA.

established.title: Inflammation as an ageing axis
established.text: "Inflammaging" is an established concept; miR-21 is described as a circulating inflammation marker (Olivieri et al. 2012).

established.title: microRNAs are stable in dried blood
established.text: microRNAs are considered more robust than mRNA and remain comparatively stable in dried samples — the sampling route itself is sound.

established.title: The established standard for biological age
established.text: That is methylation clocks: Horvath, PhenoAge, GrimAge and DunedinPACE. DunedinPACE shows high test-retest reliability and associations with morbidity and mortality.

preliminary.title: microRNA age clock
preliminary.text: The published model (n = 539) explains about 5 % of the variance in age with a mean absolute error of 10.4 years; two of the three markers did not correlate significantly with chronological age. As an age determination the value does not hold.

preliminary.title: Telomere length by qPCR
preliminary.text: The method varies considerably between runs and laboratories; DNA extraction, storage and cell composition systematically affect the result. Assay variation from dried blood is higher than from venous blood.

preliminary.title: Gene-based dietary advice
preliminary.text: The Food4Me study found no difference in weight loss between levels of personalisation including genetics. The benefit lies in structure, conversation and adherence — not in superiority over good standard counselling.

preliminary.title: microRNA as stress markers
preliminary.text: There is work on individual microRNAs and acute as well as chronic stress, but no established cut-offs and no diagnostic validation.

items.q: What is the difference between genetics and epigenetics?
items.a: Genetic variants are unchangeable for life and describe predisposition — they are recorded once. Epigenetic markers describe the current regulatory state, respond to nutrition, exercise, sleep and strain, and can therefore be measured over time. Only the epigenetic layer works as a measure of success.

A few drops of capillary blood from the fingertip go onto a dried blood card and dry there. No venipuncture, no centrifuge, no cold chain — sampling is possible in the practice or at home. The card is sent to the partner laboratory in the prepared envelope.

items.q: When does a follow-up measurement make sense?
items.a: After 4 to 6 months at the earliest and under conditions as similar as possible. The trend carries the message, not the single value — an initial and a follow-up measurement together form a plannable programme. Acute infections shift inflammation markers, so the timing should be chosen deliberately.

items.q: Do these analyses replace clinical diagnostics?
items.a: No. They are consultation and monitoring tools, not a medical diagnosis and not a substitute for clinical assessment. Where findings suggest a condition requiring treatment, the person belongs in medical or psychotherapeutic assessment.

In Germany, genetic analyses are subject to the Genetic Diagnostics Act: the person examined must be informed and give written consent before sampling, and this must be documented. It applies to Metabolic Health and to the Plus variant of Healthy Sport.

That differs by analysis, and we state it openly. The sampling route itself is sound, as is the monitoring approach. The microRNA age clock, by contrast, is exploratory, and qPCR telomere values vary considerably. The evidence sheet separates established from preliminary evidence and names the sources.
B2B terms on request, tiered by volume and contract model. There is no public consumer price list. Test cards, shipping material and report delivery are part of the offer.

items.q: Which organisations is the programme suitable for?
items.a: The analyses are supplied to professional users only: prevention and longevity practices, nutritional counselling, sports medicine and coaching, and workplace health management.

compare.caption: At a glance
compare.title: The six panels compared
compare.lead: All six panels run from the same dried blood spot card, collected from a fingertip. What differs is what is determined from it — the scope, the molecular level and the form the result takes. Epigenetic markers and microRNAs shift with diet, physical activity, sleep and stress; genetic variants remain unchanged for life. Only the epigenetic level lends itself to checking whether an intervention is working.

compare.caveatTitle: Two panels where the methodology belongs in the conversation

caveats.title: Biological Age Clock
caveats.text: The underlying model has been published as a pilot study (n = 539) and carries a mean absolute error of around 10 years. A single reading is not a determination of age; what holds up is the trend over time.

caveats.title: Telomere Analysis
caveats.text: qPCR measurement varies considerably between runs and between laboratories, more so from dried blood than from venous blood. Here too it is the trend that carries the interpretation, not the individual value. Both sample reports devote a page to this under the heading “Scientific context”.

compare.gendg: Two panels include genetic analyses: Metabolic Health and the Plus variant of Healthy Sport. For these, the person concerned must be informed and give written consent before the sample is taken (German Genetic Diagnostics Act, GenDG).

basics.caption: Understanding the values
basics.title: What the reports actually measure
basics.lead: The reports contain values from four different levels. Once the distinction is clear, it is immediately obvious which figures can change and which cannot — and which findings describe a predisposition rather than a snapshot in time. No value is a diagnosis; the analyses describe predispositions and snapshots in time.

concepts.title: The genes — the blueprint
concepts.text: The genes are rather like the blueprint of a house: they set out how the body is built — how it uses fat, how quickly satiety sets in, how well it transports vitamin D through the blood. Small deviations in this blueprint are called gene variants, or SNPs; every person carries thousands of them, and they are neither good nor bad, simply different. In Germany, genetic analyses fall under the Genetic Diagnostics Act (Gendiagnostikgesetz, GenDG) — information and written consent must be in place before the sample is taken.
concepts.key: The blueprint never changes. A genetic analysis is carried out once in a lifetime; a second measurement would return exactly the same result.

concepts.title: Methylation — the volume controls
concepts.text: The blueprint says nothing about what is being built right now. That is governed by chemical markers sitting on the DNA, which turn individual genes up or down; this system is known as methylation. It responds to diet, exercise, sleep and stress.
concepts.key: These values change. They do not show which genes someone has, but how active those genes currently are — which is what makes them suitable for monitoring progress.

concepts.title: MicroRNAs — the messengers in the blood
concepts.text: MicroRNAs are tiny molecules that circulate in the blood and fine-tune the activity of genes. They can be pictured as short messages the body sends out continuously. Their quantity shifts faster than methylation — often within weeks.
concepts.key: Their names always follow the same pattern: "miR" plus a number. The number is simply a catalogue number and says nothing about importance.

concepts.title: Telomeres — the protective caps
concepts.text: At the ends of the chromosomes sit protective caps, much like the plastic tips on shoelaces. They are called telomeres, and they prevent genetic information from being lost each time a cell divides. With every division they become a little shorter.
concepts.key: Telomeres cannot be deliberately lengthened. The only thing open to influence is how quickly they shorten.

scales.v: The most common format, also called the scale of 1 to 9 in the text. Red on the left, green on the right; higher is always better: 1–3 red, 4–6 yellow, 7–9 green.
The value in comparison with a reference group. 100 % means: precisely within the expected range.
A "biological age" calculated from measured values and set against chronological age. It is the result of a calculation, not a determination of age.
